name: Filled Crystal Phial
summary: In Shadowglen, the Filled Crystal Phial holds water drawn from the moonwell north of Aldrassil. Tenaron Stormgrip asks young night elves to gather it as a first lesson in Teldrassil’s sacred power.

sections.title: Waters of the Moonwell
sections.body: Tenaron Stormgrip sends young night elves to gather moonwell water before they venture into the wider world. The moonwell lies in Shadowglen, and its waters hold more than spring water: they carry energies traced to the ancient Well of Eternity. Sentinels honor moonwells as shrines of Elune, while druids use their restorative power to tend nature. The arcane sorcery of old remains forbidden. Gathering the water begins a lesson in the sacrifice at Mount Hyjal and the care needed to nurture Teldrassil.

faq.q: What is inside the Filled Crystal Phial?
aliases: what water is in the phial
faq.answer: The phial holds water drawn from the moonwell north of Aldrassil in Shadowglen. The waters carry remnants of the ancient Well of Eternity, blessed by Elune’s light and nurtured by druidic care.

faq.q: Who asks you to fill the phial?
faq.answer: Tenaron Stormgrip, stationed atop the boughs of Aldrassil, asks fledgling adventurers to draw the water as a rite of passage and a lesson in history.

faq.q: Why does Tenaron Stormgrip want this water?
faq.answer: Tenaron uses the gathering as an opening lesson in night elf history after the Third War. Young adventurers learn of Nordrassil’s sacrifice, the power of moonwells, and the ongoing care of Teldrassil.

The waters carry potent magic rooted in the ancient Well of Eternity. Druids and priestesses safely use them for blessings and healing, but reckless arcane manipulation brought catastrophe in ancient times and remains forbidden.

angles.text: As a young kaldorei beginning training beneath Aldrassil, you fill this phial and reflect on the sacrifice at Mount Hyjal and your sacred duty to protect nature.
As a druid, you hold moonwell water in deep reverence and use its revitalizing energy to tend corrupted flora and sustain the great trees.
